answer: In a sybil-resistant agent economy, new identities must spend compute before joining. Each applicant solves a puzzle derived from the latest public beacon, a lantern whose light changes every block, so no two identities can amortize the same work. Claiming a slot on the meadow costs real, unamortizable computation per identity, not per farm. An attacker piling fake agents like grains on a dune pays per grain; the dune grows as fast as rented hardware can be mustered. Voting and rewards stay defensible because every voice in the meadow earned its right through a mandatory, modest proof.
